whoIsThisFor.heading: Who is the Strategy Designer exam for?

personas.label: UX strategists and service designers
personas.description: You work at the strategy level — journey mapping, stakeholder alignment, and experience vision — and want to validate your ability to apply design thinking on Salesforce projects.

personas.label: Consultants leading discovery workshops
personas.description: You facilitate design workshops, conduct user research, and frame business problems for Salesforce implementation teams.

personas.label: Product owners bridging design and business
personas.description: You define experience strategy and connect design decisions to business outcomes on the Salesforce Platform.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Strategy Designer Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: The Strategy Designer exam is moderate in difficulty. It tests strategic design thinking rather than hands-on configuration — the challenge is applying design frameworks (design thinking, service blueprints, journey mapping) to Salesforce project scenarios.
bullets: ~65% passing score — you can miss up to 21 questions.
Design thinking application — expect questions that present a project scenario and ask which design thinking phase, research method, or mapping artefact is appropriate.
Business value framing — you need to connect design decisions to business metrics and present recommendations using business language rather than design terminology.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Score 75%+ on practice exams and make sure you can write a How Might We statement, distinguish journey maps from service blueprints, and frame design recommendations in business terms.

examFormat.heading: Strategy Designer Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or in-person. Here is the format:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: About 50-60% of questions are scenario-based. Common patterns include choosing the right research method for a discovery phase, selecting the correct mapping tool (journey map vs service blueprint vs ecosystem map), and framing a design recommendation for executive stakeholders.
bestWayToPass: Master design thinking phases: Know what artefacts each phase produces — empathy maps and interview notes (Empathise), problem statements and HMW questions (Define), concept sketches (Ideate), testable prototypes (Prototype), and usability findings (Test).

Know journey mapping vs service blueprints: Journey maps visualise the user's emotional arc across touchpoints. Service blueprints add backstage processes and supporting systems. Know when to use each.
Frame design in business terms: The exam tests whether you can connect UX improvements to business outcomes like reduced support volume, improved conversion rates, or shorter onboarding time.

Understand Agile UX integration: Know dual-track Agile (discovery vs delivery), Design Sprints, and Lean UX — the exam tests how to integrate UX research into agile delivery without creating a waterfall handoff.

certificationCard.description: This exam covers applying design thinking and human-centered research to shape experience strategies on the Salesforce Platform, from stakeholder alignment through journey mapping and prototyping.

keyConcepts.h2: Strategy Designer: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Human-Centered Design Strategy
blocks.body: The [Strategy Designer](/certifications/strategy-designer) cert focuses on applying **design thinking** at the strategic level — not just UI design but organisational and service design. Design thinking phases: Empathise (deep user research, stakeholder interviews, observation), Define (synthesise insights into a clear problem statement — How Might We framing), Ideate (divergent brainstorming, then convergent selection), Prototype (lo-fi representations to test concepts), Test (validate with users and iterate). The exam tests which phase a given activity belongs to and what artefacts are produced at each stage.

blocks.heading: Service Design and Journey Mapping
blocks.body: Service Blueprints map the end-to-end service experience from the customer's viewpoint (frontstage) through the supporting processes (backstage) to the enabling systems and infrastructure. They reveal moments of truth — where the service experience is won or lost. User **journey maps** visualise the emotional arc of a user experience across touchpoints and channels. Ecosystem Maps show the full web of stakeholders and their relationships. The exam tests how to choose and apply the right mapping tool for a given design challenge.

blocks.heading: Business Value Framing
blocks.body: [Strategy Designer](/certifications/strategy-designer)s must connect design decisions to business outcomes. Value Proposition Design: the Job-to-be-Done framework identifies what customers are trying to accomplish, what pains they experience, and what gains they seek — the value proposition relieves pains and creates gains. ROI of UX: reduced support volume, improved conversion rates, reduced onboarding time. Stakeholder alignment: presenting design concepts to executive sponsors using business language, not design terminology. The exam tests how to frame design decisions in terms of business metrics and stakeholder concerns.

blocks.heading: Agile UX: Design Sprints and Dual-Track
blocks.body: Dual-track **Agile** separates discovery (what to build) from delivery (how to build it). Discovery track: continuous research, prototype testing, and backlog refinement. Delivery track: sprint development of validated features. Design Sprints (Google Ventures model): 5-day intensive to solve a design challenge from definition to user-tested prototype. Lean UX: minimise waste by building the smallest testable increment. The exam tests how to integrate UX research into agile delivery without creating a waterfall design handoff.

blocks.heading: Ethics, Inclusion, and Responsible Design
blocks.body: [Strategy Designer](/certifications/strategy-designer)s bear responsibility for the impact of the solutions they recommend. Inclusive design: design for the full spectrum of human diversity — ability, age, culture, language. Dark patterns in UX: manipulative design that tricks users into unintended actions — the strategy designer advocates against these. AI ethics in Salesforce products: fairness, transparency, accountability, and human control (Einstein's Trusted AI principles apply here). The exam tests how to identify design decisions that could cause harm and how to advocate for more equitable alternatives.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Strategy Designer Exam
scenarioTips.intro: The Strategy Designer exam tests design thinking and human-centered design applied to Salesforce projects. Focus on research methods, journey mapping, problem framing, and how to facilitate design workshops.

blocks.heading: Design Thinking Process
blocks.body: Know the five-stage **design thinking** process: Empathize, Define, Ideate, Prototype, Test. Understand when to apply each stage and how to move between stages iteratively based on research findings.

blocks.heading: Research Methods
blocks.body: Know quantitative vs. qualitative research methods: surveys, interviews, contextual inquiry, diary studies, and usability testing. Know how to select the right method based on the research question.

blocks.heading: Journey Mapping
blocks.body: Know how to create current-state and future-state **journey maps**: identifying touchpoints, emotions, pain points, and opportunities. Understand the difference between journey maps, service blueprints, and experience maps.

blocks.heading: Problem Framing & HMW Statements
blocks.body: Know how to write 'How Might We' (HMW) statements that reframe problems as opportunities. Understand how to use the POV (Point of View) statement to align on the design challenge.

blocks.heading: Facilitation Techniques
blocks.body: Know how to facilitate design workshops: affinity mapping, dot voting, crazy 8s ideation, and how to use the Lightning Decision Jam framework to move from problem to solution efficiently.
